title: Budget Billing — Plan Activation, Withdrawal and Closure of Service
content:
# Budget Billing — Plan Activation, Withdrawal and Closure of Service

**Rule.** The customer may leave a Budget Billing plan at any time; the withdrawal takes effect on the next regular bill after the request and the deferred balance is settled under the plan's withdrawal settlement terms, and a FlatBill left early settles actual charges against FlatBill amounts where the plan provides an early-exit true-up. Leaving a plan is the customer's own decision. When the service agreement closes the plan closes and settles under the plan's service closure settlement terms; a plan that moves with the customer is instead re-enrolled on the customer's new agreement with its deferred balance settled on the final bill. The plan becomes active on the first regular bill issued after enrollment.

## Questions the rule answers

**When does a plan begin?** A plan is enrolled when the customer chooses it, and becomes active when the first regular bill issued after enrollment is issued carrying the plan installment. Its activation is dated on the bill date of that first plan bill.

**Can the customer leave before the first plan bill?** Yes. A customer may leave at any time, including while the plan is enrolled and before its first plan bill; the plan then ends as withdrawn without having become active.

**When does a withdrawal take effect?** On the next regular bill after the request. The withdrawal is dated on the date it takes effect.

**What happens to the deferred balance on withdrawal?** It is settled under the plan's withdrawal settlement terms. On the levelized and budget plans the deferred balance is billed or credited on the next regular bill. On a FlatBill left before its term ends, the actual charges of the term to date are settled against the FlatBill amounts billed in that term.

**Who decides to leave?** The customer. Leaving a plan is the customer's own decision.

**What happens when the service agreement closes?** The plan closes with it, dated on the stop date of the service agreement, and its deferred balance is settled under the plan's service closure settlement terms, on the final bill.

**What if the customer is moving to a new address?** Where the plan moves with the customer — the Residential Levelized Billing Plan and the Residential Budget Billing Plan — the plan is re-enrolled on the customer's new service agreement, and the deferred balance of the old agreement is settled on its final bill. The Commercial Levelized Billing Plan, the Commercial Budget Billing Plan and the two FlatBill plans do not move; when their agreement closes they close and settle under their service closure settlement terms.

## Hypothetical illustrations

| Situation | Outcome |
|---|---|
| Residential Budget Billing Plan customer asks to leave on 3 June; the next regular bill is dated 11 June | Withdrawal takes effect on the 11 June bill; the deferred balance is billed or credited on the next regular bill |
| Residential FlatBill Plan customer leaves in month 8 of the term; actual charges of the term to date $1,044.60, FlatBill amounts billed $1,016.00 | $28.60 billed as the early-exit true-up |
| Residential Levelized Billing Plan customer stops service at one address and starts service at another | Plan re-enrolled on the new agreement; the old agreement's deferred balance settled on its final bill |
| Commercial Levelized Billing Plan customer closes one site | Plan closes with that agreement; deferred balance billed or credited on its final bill |
